chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about voluntary prayer during the day while I was traveling. He said, 'No, but you make up the night prayer during the day while you are traveling.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, regarding the daytime prayer that I pray when resident, do I make it up during the day while traveling?' He said, 'As for me, I do not make it up.'

As for the report narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Do I make up the daytime prayer at night while traveling?' He said, 'Yes.' Then Isma'il ibn Jabir asked him, 'Do I make up the daytime prayer at night while traveling?' He said, 'No.' Isma'il said, 'You said Yes.' He said, 'That one is able [to do it], and you are not able.'

This is to be understood as: if he made it up, he would not be sinful, even if it is not a prescribed Sunnah, or perhaps he knew of his condition that if he did not command him to do so, he would slight the Sunnahs, and that would lead to neglecting the obligatory duties. So he commanded him to do so to strengthen his inclination towards maintaining the prayers. And he knew of the condition of the other that it was the opposite, so he commanded him to leave the repetition, even though the report does not explicitly state that he may pray the voluntary daytime prayers or their obligatory counterparts at night. And if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as referring to the obligatory prayers. And if it had explicitly mentioned the voluntary prayers, it would not have meant that they were missed while he was traveling, or missed while he was resident. And if it can be interpreted that way, we interpret it as referring to one who missed the voluntary prayers while resident; it is permissible for him to make them up while traveling at night. And that which clarifies that the repetition of the voluntary daytime prayer is not a prescribed Sunnah.
ai.seo_question: Can a traveler make up missed voluntary daytime prayers at night?
ai.summary: This passage from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle of *khilaf al-mashayikh* (difference in rulings based on the individual) by contrasting Imam al-Rida’s general stance with specific instructions given to Muawiya ibn Ammar and Isma'il ibn Jabr. The commentary elucidates that the Imam’s varying answers were not contradictory but tailored to each companion’s spiritual disposition to prevent negligence in obligatory duties, illustrating the practical wisdom (*hikmah*) behind fiqh. This underscores the Shia view that voluntary acts are flexible and context-dependent, unlike the fixed nature of obligatory prayers.
